Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is generally fine to bring on a flight, as long as you carry it in your carry-on and not in checked luggage.

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 watt-hours (Wh) each. [FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)
- To check the Wh, divide mAh by 1,000 to get Ah, then multiply by the voltage. At a typical 3.7 V, 20,000 mAh works out to about 74 Wh, well under 100 Wh. The FAA explains the math on the same page.
- Example: the Baseus Blade H1 is listed at 20,000 mAh (about 74 Wh nominal) and described as carry-on legal. ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah))

**Rules to follow**
- **Carry-on only.** Spare batteries and power banks are not allowed in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over exposed terminals, so it can't short-circuit. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **No damaged or recalled units.** These can't go on the plane at all, in carry-on or checked bags. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Check your airline.** Airlines can set stricter limits, including on how many power banks you can bring. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Look for the Wh rating** printed on the battery. Some higher-voltage or unusual designs may differ from the 3.7 V assumption.
